long_biography.plain_text:
McGraw studied psychology at the University of Texas before earning a law degree from Southern Methodist University. He first wrote advice books for teenagers, then developed publishing businesses that released work by other authors.

Television became the main operating thread. McGraw created The Doctors as a syndicated programme built around practising clinicians and served as its executive producer through a long run. His production slate later expanded across scripted drama and factual entertainment, including Bull and DailyMailTV. He also helped establish Doctor On Demand, a telehealth service that subsequently combined with Grand Rounds and adopted the Included Health name. These ventures distinguish his own company-building record from the audience access provided by the wider McGraw media business.
